subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Decaf: How It Works
description: A micro-lesson that makes Decaf: How It Works usable.

hook.text: Decaf coffee still contains about 3% of the original caffeine. True zero-caffeine coffee doesn't exist.

buildup.text: Swiss Water Process soaks green beans in water to dissolve caffeine, then filters it out with carbon.

discovery.text: Supercritical CO₂ extraction uses pressurized carbon dioxide as a selective solvent—targeting only caffeine.

twist.text: Early decaf methods used chemical solvents. Some critics still distrust decaf because of that history.

climax.text: Modern decaf quality has improved dramatically. Blind tastings show many people can't tell the difference.

punchline.text: Same bean, minus the buzz. Science got surprisingly good at this.

quiz.question: What does the Swiss Water Process use to remove caffeine?

details.summary: Decaffeination removes 97 percent or more of caffeine from green beans before roasting. The three main methods use chemical solvents, supercritical CO2, or water. Each method affects flavor differently, and modern processes are far better at preserving taste than earlier techniques.
details.whyItMatters: Decaf has long suffered a reputation for poor flavor. Understanding the methods helps consumers find decaf they actually enjoy.
takeaways: Decaf retains at least 97 percent caffeine removal
Swiss Water Process uses no chemical solvents
CO2 processing preserves the most original flavor

faq.question: Is the Swiss Water Process really chemical free?
faq.answer: Yes. The Swiss Water Process uses only water, temperature, and time to remove caffeine. Green beans soak in water saturated with coffee solubles except caffeine. Osmosis draws caffeine out of the beans while other compounds stay. No chemical solvents are used.

faq.question: Does decaf coffee have any caffeine at all?
faq.answer: Decaf is not completely caffeine-free. A typical 8-ounce cup contains 2 to 15 milligrams of caffeine compared to 80 to 100 milligrams in regular coffee. For most people this trace amount has no noticeable effect.
